# Department of Commerce total outlays (on-budget + off-budget) for FY 2016-2024
# Values in millions from the Treasury Bulletin tables

outlays = {
    2016: 9162,
    2017: 10303,
    2018: 8561,
    2019: 11326,
    2020: 15918,
    2021: 13135,
    2022: 11734,
    2023: 12045,
    2024: 14831
}

# Print the values
print("Department of Commerce Total Outlays (millions):")
for year, value in outlays.items():
    print(f"FY {year}: {value}")

# Create sorted list of values
values = sorted(outlays.values())
print(f"\nSorted values: {values}")

# Tukey exclusive median method for Q1:
# 1. Find median
# 2. For Q1, use lower half (excluding median if odd number of points)
# The median of odd-length data is the middle value
# For Q1, we use the median of the lower half

n = len(values)
print(f"\nn = {n}")

# Find median
if n % 2 == 0:
    median = (values[n//2 - 1] + values[n//2]) / 2
    lower_half = values[:n//2]
    upper_half = values[n//2:]
else:
    median = values[n//2]
    # For Tukey exclusive, exclude the median from both halves
    lower_half = values[:n//2]
    upper_half = values[n//2 + 1:]

print(f"Median (Tukey exclusive): {median}")
print(f"Lower half (exclusive of median): {lower_half}")
print(f"Upper half (exclusive of median): {upper_half}")

# Q1 is the median of the lower half
m = len(lower_half)
if m % 2 == 0:
    q1 = (lower_half[m//2 - 1] + lower_half[m//2]) / 2
else:
    q1 = lower_half[m//2]

print(f"\nQ1 (Tukey exclusive method) = {q1}")
print(f"Rounded to nearest hundredths: {q1:.2f}")
EOF
